players.product: Photosensitive materials for advanced photoresists (Photosensitive Materials segment); high-purity solvents for advanced logic and memory

quarterly_data.quarter: Toyo Gosei annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 (annual securities report): demand for materials for advanced semiconductors grew and sales of materials for advanced photoresists and of high-purity solvents (Chemicals segment) were strong, so net sales rose to JPY 41,956 million (+JPY 3,291 million, +8.5%). Operating profit fell to JPY 3,668 million (-JPY 434 million, -10.6%), ordinary profit to JPY 3,592 million (-10.1%) and net income to JPY 2,692 million (-17.9%): depreciation and fixed costs such as added headcount rose sharply from the start of the year as the large facility for advanced semiconductor materials and the production information system started operation, and higher sales of high-value-added products in the second half absorbed part of the increase. Management states demand for AI-related semiconductor devices kept driving the electronic materials market, expanding further especially toward the second half.
quarterly_data.figure: Net sales JPY 41,956 million (+8.5%); operating profit JPY 3,668 million (-10.6%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Toyo Gosei annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Segments, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): Photosensitive Materials net sales JPY 26,417 million (+10.7%) - sales of materials for advanced photoresists rose on continued strong demand for AI semiconductor devices while materials for general semiconductors fell slightly, and photosensitive materials for displays stayed steady; segment operating profit JPY 1,051 million (-46.9%) on the higher fixed costs of the large facility and production information system. Chemicals net sales JPY 15,538 million (+5.0%), operating profit JPY 2,617 million (+23.2%) - high-purity solvent demand expanded mainly for advanced logic and memory; fragrance materials fell on supply-chain inventory adjustments caused by US tariff measures and on currency effects; the tank-terminal contract rate stayed high, helped by a new tank dedicated to inorganic chemicals. Production (at selling prices): Photosensitive Materials JPY 32,778 million (+12.5%), Chemicals JPY 15,883 million (+0.4%), total JPY 48,661 million (+8.2%); the company states it in principle produces to forecast (no orders figures are given). Sales by region: Japan JPY 29,202 million, China and Taiwan JPY 6,200 million, Asia excluding China and Taiwan JPY 2,930 million, North America JPY 3,014 million, Europe JPY 491 million, other JPY 116 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Photosensitive Materials JPY 26,417 million (+10.7%); Chemicals JPY 15,538 million (+5.0%); production JPY 48,661 million (+8.2%)

quarterly_data.quarter: Toyo Gosei annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and capex (annual securities report): capex in the year to March 2026 was JPY 4,336 million (Photosensitive Materials JPY 1,274 million, Chemicals JPY 2,345 million), mainly capacity expansion, efficiency and R&D. Management states it is using the expanded fourth photosensitive materials plant and the development and analysis building to raise supply capacity for leading-edge products, and the Awaji Plant's second indoor filling station to raise high-purity solvent shipping capacity and quality; it is preparing to build a new photosensitive materials plant to expand supply capacity for advanced-semiconductor materials and has acquired land for future business, and for high-purity solvents it has started building a new tank yard and tank-lorry filling station and acquired land for future capacity expansion. Plan for the year after March 31, 2026: about JPY 4,460 million of significant new facilities and upgrades (Photosensitive Materials JPY 1,450 million, Chemicals JPY 3,010 million; expansion, rationalisation and maintenance). The Chiba Plant (photosensitive materials production) had a book value of JPY 25,386 million and 585 employees at March 31, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: Capex JPY 4,336 million; next-year plan about JPY 4,460 million (Photosensitive Materials JPY 1,450 million, Chemicals JPY 3,010 million)

quarterly_data.quarter: Toyo Gosei annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management outlook (annual securities report): management expects medium- to long-term demand growth for advanced materials used in semiconductor manufacturing, given the strategic importance of semiconductors to many countries and growing communications and data-center demand as generative AI spreads; it puts stable supply first (multiple sourcing of raw materials, inventory) and plans to review selling prices through talks with customers to address higher raw-material, fuel and logistics costs. The five-year 'Beyond 500' medium-term plan (started in the year to March 2023) targets, for its final year, net sales of JPY 500 hundred million or more, operating profit of JPY 80 hundred million or more and an operating margin of 16% or more; its segment strategy includes sufficient capacity investment for the Photosensitive Materials segment and stronger quality, development and stable-supply systems for ultra-high-purity solvents for advanced semiconductors.
quarterly_data.figure: Final-year targets: operating margin 16% or more

quarterly_data.quarter: Toyo Gosei annual securities report: FY2026 (06-23-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D, year to March 2026 (annual securities report): R&D expenses JPY 1,795 million. Photosensitive Materials: developing and industrialising photosensitive materials (raw materials for photoresists) for highly integrated semiconductor devices and FPDs; in its core chemically amplified resist materials, R&D includes materials for EUV resists used in advanced semiconductor processes, with leading-edge LSI requiring strict control of metal impurities and of every manufacturing step. Chemicals: high-purity solvents R&D centres on manufacturing and recycling methods, with product development alongside customer companies for the stricter quality that further scaling of integrated circuits will require. New fields: photo-nanoimprint resins supplied in Japan and abroad for AR device development and mass production, and photosensitive biocompatible polymers for cell-culture and diagnostic uses.
